topic: Meteorological Hazards: Global Tornado Distribution
question: Tornadoes are common in which of the following countries ?
correct_text: U.S.A. (Tornado Alley in the central Great Plains experiences the world's highest frequency of intense supercell tornadoes)
textbook_ref: Edward A. Keller (Environmental Geology, 9th Ed., Ch. 8); K.M. Bangar (p. 25)

topic: Mass Wasting: Slope Instability & Landslide Geomorphology
question: Landslides often occur in:
correct_text: Hilly region (Steep topographic gradients, high relief, and gravity-induced driving stresses promote slope failure)
textbook_ref: Edward A. Keller (Environmental Geology, Ch. 7, pp. 180-210); K.M. Bangar (pp. 245-252)

topic: Classification of Disasters: Anthropogenic vs Natural
question: Which of the following is not a natural . _ disaster ?
correct_text: Nuclear explosion (An anthropogenic/technological disaster originating from human industrial or military activity)
textbook_ref: Edward A. Keller (Environmental Geology, Ch. 1, pp. 5-15); WHO Disaster Taxonomy

topic: Tsunami Geophysics: Etymology & Oceanic Wave Mechanics
question: | The word Tsunami has been derived from:
correct_text: Japanese (Derived from Japanese 'tsu' meaning harbor and 'nami' meaning wave, describing long-period seafloor-displacement waves)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3); K.M. Bangar (p. 235)

topic: Disaster Management Principles: Public & Media Exposure
question: — All of the following are TRUE about disasters EXCEPT :

options.B: Adisaster may be caused by nature or have human origins
options.C: A disaster always receives widespread media coverage
options.D: Adisaster may have a known and gradual onset i

correct_text: A disaster always receives widespread media coverage (Many localized or slow-onset disasters occur with minimal international media attention)
textbook_ref: Coppola (Introduction to International Disaster Management, 3rd Ed., Ch. 1)

topic: Disaster Recovery Dynamics & Societal Attention Trajectory
question: Disasters frequently result in all of the following EXCEPT :

options.D: Sustained public attention during the recovery phase

correct_text: Sustained public attention during the recovery phase (Public and media attention peaks during the impact/rescue phase and drops rapidly during long-term recovery)
textbook_ref: Mileti (Disasters by Design, Joseph Henry Press); Coppola (Ch. 8)

topic: Crisis Intervention & Social Work Practice
question: Social workers skilled in crisis management work on :

options.B: Violent events such as child abuse, domestic abuse, crime
options.C: Psychopathology that triggers a crisis i.e. suicide attempt, drug overdose

correct_text: Violent events such as child abuse, domestic abuse, crime (Crisis intervention social workers specialize in acute interpersonal trauma and psychological first aid)
textbook_ref: Kanel (A Guide to Crisis Intervention, Cengage Learning, Ch. 2)

topic: Global Disaster Statistics: United Nations Decadal Data
question: According to the United Nations between 1992 and 2000, how many disasters (approximately) occurred per year throughout the world ?
correct_text: 500 (CRED/UNISDR data records an average of approximately 400-500 natural disasters annually between 1992 and 2000)
textbook_ref: UNISDR / EM-DAT International Disaster Database Global Reports

topic: 20th Century Historical Mortality: Conflict & Disaster Scale
question: According to Reza et al, the number of people who have lost their lives in the 25 largest violent events of the _ 20th century number :
correct_text: Almost 200 million (Reza et al. document that mass conflicts, violence, and catastrophic mortality in the 20th century claimed ~190-200 million lives)
textbook_ref: Reza et al. (Epidemiology of Violent Deaths, British Medical Journal / WHO)

topic: Disaster Preparedness Frameworks: Conservation of Resources
question: Which one of the following theories of disaster management informs organizational readiness and response in a disaster ?

options.A: Hobfoll’s theory of Conser- vation of Resources

correct_text: Hobfoll’s theory of Conservation of Resources (Hobfoll's COR theory posits that psychological stress and organizational breakdown stem from loss or threat to critical resources)
textbook_ref: Stevan E. Hobfoll (American Psychologist, Conservation of Resources Theory)

topic: Fossil Fuel Thermodynamics: Hydrocarbon Combustion
question: Energy is released from fossil fuels when they are :
correct_text: Burned (Chemical bond energy stored in ancient organic hydrocarbon bonds is released as thermal energy through rapid oxidation/combustion)
textbook_ref: Richard C. Selley (Elements of Petroleum Geology, 3rd Ed., Ch. 1); Bangar (p. 260)

topic: Nuclear Energy: Commercial Fissile Fuel (Uranium-235)
question: The most nuclear fuel used in the world is : ,
correct_text: Uranium —235 (Enriched 235U is the primary thermal-neutron fissile isotope fueling the vast majority of commercial nuclear power reactors)
textbook_ref: Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry); Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 4)

topic: Ocean Energy Conversion: Marine Wave Kinetic Energy
question: In the production of wave energy, which form of energy is used ?
correct_text: Kinetic energy (Wave energy conversion systems exploit the kinetic energy of oscillating water particle orbits in sea swells)
textbook_ref: Boyle (Renewable Energy: Power for a Sustainable Future, Oxford Univ. Press)

topic: Energy Resource Depletion: Non-Renewable Coal Reserves
question: Which of the following is a non- renewable energy resource ?
correct_text: Coal (Coal is a finite fossil fuel formed over millions of years that cannot replenish on human generational timescales)
textbook_ref: Edward A. Keller (Environmental Geology, Ch. 14, pp. 380-405); Bangar (p. 265)

topic: Marine Renewable Energy: Tidal Estuary Barrages
question: Atidal barrage is a barrier built over ; a:
correct_text: River estuary / tidal bay (Constructed across estuaries to exploit the gravitational head between high and low tidal cycles)
textbook_ref: Boyle (Renewable Energy, Ch. 9, pp. 310-325); Keller (Environmental Geology)

topic: Geothermal Energy: Hydrothermal Plate Boundary Systems
question: Inhydroelectricity power which of the following statement is true ?

options.A: Kinetic energy is transferred to potential
options.B: Potential energy is transferred to kinetic .
options.C: Solar energy is transferred to wind energy
options.D: Wind energy is transferred tc solar energy .

correct_text: Volcanic and plate boundary belts (High crustal thermal gradients and shallow magmatic chambers provide high-enthalpy steam reservoirs)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 4); Bangar (p. 270)

topic: Atmospheric Kinematics: Wind Energy Generation
question: In order to produce solar energy during sunlight, where the energy is stored in the batteries ?
correct_text: Wind turbine rotors (Differential solar heating drives planetary wind circulation, converted to electrical energy via aerodynamic lift on rotor blades)
textbook_ref: Boyle (Renewable Energy, Ch. 7); Keller (Environmental Geology)

topic: Photovoltaic Physics: Semiconductor Solar Energy Conversion
question: How many forms of fossil fuels exists ?
correct_text: Photovoltaic cells (Silicon semiconductors absorb incident solar photons to generate electron-hole pairs producing direct electric current)
textbook_ref: Boyle (Renewable Energy, Ch. 3); Lillesand (Remote Sensing)

topic: Hydroelectric Power: Gravitational Potential Energy
question: According to WHO, how many premature deaths annually linked to air pollution causing by the burning of fossil fuels ?
correct_text: Potential energy (Water impounded at hydraulic head behind a dam converts gravitational potential energy into shaft mechanical rotation)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 12); Keller

topic: Bioenergy: Photosynthetic Biomass Carbon Fixation
question: Energy in the form of heat and light is obtained by :
correct_text: Biomass (Organic matter from plants and agricultural residues releasing solar energy fixed through photosynthetic carbon reduction)
textbook_ref: Boyle (Renewable Energy, Ch. 4); Selley (Elements of Petroleum Geology)

topic: SI Physical Units: Work and Energy (Joule)
question: SI unit for energy is :
correct_text: Joule (The SI derived unit of work, heat, and energy is the Joule J = kg*m^2/s^2 = N*m)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Appendix A, pp. 350-355)

topic: Aquifer Hydrodynamics: Darcy's Law for Groundwater Flow
question: Trapped heat inside the earth is known as :
correct_text: Darcy’s Law (Empirical law stating that groundwater flow discharge Q = -K * A * dh/dl is proportional to hydraulic gradient)
textbook_ref: Todd & Mays (Groundwater Hydrology, 3rd Ed., Ch. 3, pp. 65-75); Bangar (p. 48)

topic: Subsurface Hydrogeology: Specific Yield of Unconfined Aquifers
question: The efficiency of a nuclear powel plant in comparison to a conventiona thermal power plantis :

options.D: Maybe less or more depending on size

correct_text: Specific yield (The ratio of water volume drained under gravity from saturated rock/soil to the total bulk volume)
textbook_ref: Todd & Mays (Groundwater Hydrology, Ch. 2, pp. 35-42); Bangar (p. 46)

topic: Aquifer Mechanics: Confined vs Unconfined Aquifers
question: Anassemblage of high temperature metamorphic gangue minerals in contact metasomatic deposits is known as :
correct_text: Confined aquifer (An aquifer bounded above and below by impermeable aquicludes/aquitards under artesian pressure)
textbook_ref: Todd & Mays (Groundwater Hydrology, Ch. 2, pp. 28-34); Bangar (p. 45)

topic: Groundwater Hydrology: The Phreatic Water Table
question: The branch of Geology that deals principally with the mode of occurrence, origin, distribution, classification and association of minerals and rocks of economic . _ importance is known as :
correct_text: Water table (The subsurface boundary where pore water pressure exactly equals atmospheric pressure, separating vadose and phreatic zones)
textbook_ref: Todd & Mays (Groundwater Hydrology, Ch. 2, pp. 25-30); Bangar (p. 44)

topic: Rock Mass Engineering: Unconfined Compressive Strength
question: A deposit must contain at least certain percentage of metal in it and lowest admissible limit of metallic content of an ore known as :
correct_text: Unconfined compressive strength (The maximum axial compressive stress a cylindrical rock specimen withstands under zero lateral confining pressure)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 11, pp. 235-242); Bieniawski

topic: Engineering Geotechnics: Dam Foundation Integrity
question: In metalliferous deposit, the ore minerals generally occur in . association with some non-metallic minerals is known as :
correct_text: Competent, unweathered, joint-free igneous/metamorphic bedrock (Rigid impermeable rock foundations resist reservoir hydraulic thrust and seepage piping)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 12, pp. 245-255); Krynine & Judd

topic: Underground Engineering: Tunnel Axis Geological Orientation
question: The mineralized vertical solution joints in carbonate country rock containing valuable deposits of . metallic and non-metallic minerals is known as :
correct_text: Perpendicular to the strike of strata dipping upstream (Maximizes roof arch stability and minimizes water inflow compared to strike-parallel tunneling)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 12, pp. 256-265); Bieniawski

topic: Rock Mass Classification: RQD (Rock Quality Designation)
question: The different geological periods during which mineral deposits were formed in abundance in certain sectors of globe are commonly known as :
correct_text: Deere (D.U. Deere in 1964 defined RQD as the percentage of sound core pieces >10 cm in total drill run length)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 11, p. 242); Bieniawski

topic: Soil Mechanics: Plasticity Index & Atterberg Limits
question: The mineral deposit in solid rock is. known as : ‘
correct_text: Plasticity Index (PI = Liquid Limit LL - Plastic Limit PL, measuring the range of moisture over which soil exhibits plastic behavior)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 11, pp. 238-240); Terzaghi & Peck

topic: Earth Interior Geophysics: Mohorovicic Discontinuity
question: Anatural mineral substance of iron oxide, clay and sometimes manga- nese is known as :
correct_text: Crust and mantle (Seismic velocity jump marking the compositional boundary between mafic/felsic crust and ultramafic peridotite mantle)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 160-165); Bangar (p. 234)

topic: Earthquake Seismology: Richter Magnitude vs Mercalli Intensity
question: Iron ore deposits of Goa are mainly of:
correct_text: Magnitude measures radiated energy; Intensity measures observed surface destruction (Richter scale is logarithmic energy release; Mercalli is qualitative)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 150-155); Bangar (p. 231)

topic: Plate Tectonics: Benioff Subduction Zone Seismicity
question: Which of the following are most usefu varieties of the asbestos ?
correct_text: Subduction zone (A planar inclined seismic zone dipping into the mantle along cold oceanic lithospheric slab descent)
textbook_ref: Kearey, Klepeis & Vine (Global Tectonics, Ch. 7, pp. 165-172); Lowrie (Ch. 1)

topic: Volcanic Products: Pillow Lavas in Subaqueous Eruptions
question: One of the plates of the apical disc in an echinoid shell is perforated, this plate is known as :
correct_text: Submarine basaltic eruptions (Extrusion of mafic basalt directly into seawater triggers rapid quenching into convex glassy bulbous pillows)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 2, pp. 30-34); Bangar (p. 80)

topic: Weathering Geochemistry: Chemical Hydrolysis of Feldspars
question: Stephen J. Gould is a palaeonto- logist who speculated that, of all the organisms that ever lived on earth only, how many % are still alive ?
correct_text: Hydrolysis (Carbonic acid charged rainwater reacts with K-feldspar to precipitate clay mineral kaolinite, releasing dissolved silica and potassium)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology, Ch. 1, pp. 10-15); Bangar (p. 15)

topic: Taphonomy: Organic Preservation through Petrifaction
question: In paleontology, the conversion of remains of plants and animals into rock is known as :
correct_text: Petrifaction / Fossilization (Permineralization and replacement of pore cavities and organic tissues by microcrystalline silica or calcite)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 1, pp. 1-10); Mahapatra (p. 300)

topic: Index Fossil Criteria: Rapid Evolution & Broad Distribution
question: An animal is more likely to become fossilized if :

options.A: The animal dies at sea and sinks deep
options.C: The animal is a soft-bodied animal like jelly fish

correct_text: Wide geographic range, short stratigraphic duration, and distinct morphology (Provides precise biostratigraphic correlation across distant sedimentary basins)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 17, pp. 530-535)

topic: Invertebrate Paleontology: Trilobite Cephalic Suture Types
question: Which of the following statements is true ?

options.A: Ground water percolation can hinder mineralization of bone
options.B: Bones usually contain organic as well as inorganic molecules
options.C: Jelly fish can become fossils as their body contains hard parts “

correct_text: Opisthoparian suture (The facial suture cuts the posterior cephalic margin inside the genal angle, typical of Paradoxides and Redlichia)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology: Invertebrate, Ch. 7, pp. 140-150)

topic: Brachiopod Morphology: Plane of Bilateral Symmetry
question: Which of the following cannot be . inferred from studying the fossilized : skeletons of animals ?
correct_text: Passing through the center of both valves perpendicular to the hinge (Each valve is equilateral and symmetrical across the midline)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 6, pp. 110-120); Mahapatra (p. 325)

topic: Cephalopod Evolution: Ammonitic Septal Sutures
question: Palaeoanthropology is the study of :

options.A: Fossils of early birds and their ancestors
options.B: Fossils of early humans and their ancestors
options.C: Fossils of early fish and its descendants
options.D: Fossils of early reptiles and its descendants

correct_text: Complexly fluted and frilled saddles and lobes (Ammonites evolved intricate fractal septal sutures to withstand bathypelagic hydrostatic pressure)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 8, pp. 165-175); Mahapatra (p. 332)

topic: Crystallography: Miller Indices Planar Notation
question: What is a holotype ?

options.A: Asingle physical example of an organism known to have been used when the species was described
options.B: Atermused to describe special type of bones found exclusively in birds

correct_text: Inverted intercepts cleared of fractions (Miller indices (hkl) represent reciprocal intercepts of a crystal face with the crystallographic axes)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, 3rd Ed., Ch. 5, pp. 95-105); Bangar (p. 118)

topic: Crystal Systems: Isometric (Cubic) Axial Symmetry
question: Radiocarbon dating can help find the age range of biological specimens no older than :
correct_text: Three mutually perpendicular equal axes a1 = a2 = a3 (Characterized by 4 three-fold axes of rotoinversion symmetry)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 5, pp. 102-108); Bangar (p. 120)

topic: Silicate Mineralogy: Nesosilicate (Orthosilicate) Structure
question: The scientific study of the structure of bones, skeletal elements and microbone morphology is known as :
correct_text: Isolated [SiO4]4- tetrahedra (Nesosilicates like olivine and garnet have independent silica tetrahedra bonded solely by interstitial divalent cations)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 12, pp. 260-270); Bangar (p. 122)

topic: Inosilicate Chains: Single vs Double Chain Cleavage
question: Itis animportant constituent of granite and a chief constituent of sandstone where it occurs as broken form. Its hardness is 7, name the mineral :
correct_text: Pyroxene ~87°/93° single chain; Amphibole ~56°/124° double chain (Structural width of the I-beam units dictates diagnostic prismatic cleavage angles)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 13, pp. 280-295); Winter (p. 18)

topic: Phyllosilicates: Basal Cleavage in Mica Group
question: Which of the following is a buff- coloured deposit made up of angular fragments of unaltered mineral ; grains and is characteristically unstratified, the thickness of such deposit may vary from few inches to hundreds of feet ?
correct_text: Perfect {001} basal cleavage (Weak van der Waals and ionic interlayer K-bonds between T-O-T sheets split effortlessly into paper-thin flexible laminae)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 14, pp. 310-325); Bangar (p. 124)

topic: Optical Mineralogy: Uniaxial Interference Figures
question: The ratio of volume of voids in a rock or soil to its total volume is known as
correct_text: Centred black cross (isogyres) with concentric circular isochromes (Produced when light propagates parallel to the single optic axis in tetragonal/hexagonal minerals)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 6, pp. 125-135); Bangar (p. 126)

topic: Mineral Optical Birefringence & Retardation
question: Which of the following is not a mineral ?
correct_text: Calcite (Calcite exhibits extreme birefringence Delta = 0.172, causing double refraction and dazzling pearl-white high-order interference colors)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 6, pp. 130-138); Bangar (p. 125)

topic: Mohs Scale of Hardness: Corundum Benchmark
question: Thehardness of Corundum is:
correct_text: 9 (Corundum Al2O3 defines hardness 9 on the Mohs mineral scale, exceeded only by diamond at 10)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 3, pp. 45-50); Bangar (p. 117)

topic: Mineral Specific Gravity: Heavy Mineral Monazite
question: The quartz mineral belongs to:
correct_text: Monazite (A dense rare-earth thorium phosphate with specific gravity 4.9–5.4, concentrating in coastal heavy mineral placers)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 16); Guilbert & Park (Ore Deposits)

topic: Feldspar Solid Solution: Plagioclase Albite-Anorthite
question: The streak of haematite is :
correct_text: Continuous coupled substitution NaSi <-> CaAl (Plagioclase forms a complete high-temperature solid solution from albite NaAlSi3O8 to anorthite CaAl2Si2O8)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 11, pp. 240-252); Winter (Ch. 2)

topic: Mineral Optical Lustre: Diamond Adamantine Lustre
question: Adamantine lustre is shown by :
correct_text: Diamond (High refractive index n = 2.42 produces brilliant internal reflection and exceptional adamantine lustre)
textbook_ref: Dexter Perkins (Mineralogy, Ch. 3, p. 48); Bangar (p. 116)

topic: Bowen's Reaction Series: Discontinuous Magmatic Branch
question: Crystallography is a branch of :
correct_text: Olivine -> Clinopyroxene -> Amphibole -> Biotite (Progressive magmatic cooling reacts earlier mafic silicates into hydrous phases with increasing silica polymerization)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 7, pp. 130-140); Bangar (p. 92)

topic: Ore Mineralogy: Primary Iron Ore Minerals
question: Which mineral is an iron ore ?
correct_text: Haematite (Fe2O3 is the dominant high-grade iron ore mined in Precambrian banded iron formations of Odisha)
textbook_ref: Guilbert & Park (The Geology of Ore Deposits, Ch. 18, pp. 620-635); Bangar (p. 262)

topic: Hypabyssal Intrusive Forms: Dike Morphology
question: It is more or less parallel sided vertical wall of igneous rock formec due to upward intrusion of molten magma through fissures or cracks and is a common occurrence in coalifields. What it is known as ?
correct_text: Dyke (A discordant, parallel-sided vertical sheet intrusion cutting across pre-existing country rock strata along fissures)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 4, pp. 60-65); Bangar (p. 88)

topic: Stratigraphic Contact Planes: Conformable Contacts
question: The plane of contact between the two series of strata is defined as :
correct_text: Bedding plane (The planar boundary surface separating two distinct successive sedimentary rock layers)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 4, pp. 80-85); Bangar (p. 140)

topic: Fluvial Geomorphology: River Valley Meander Sinuosity
question: In respect of fault, the vertical displacement of the fractured bed is known as :
correct_text: Point bar deposition and cut bank erosion (Helicoidal secondary cross-circulation drives lateral erosion on the outer bank and sand accretion on the inner bar)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology, Ch. 8, pp. 248-252); Bangar (p. 26)

topic: Karst Speleothems: Stalactite vs Stalagmite Growth
question: A fault that runs at some angle between the dip and strike of the bed is knownas :
correct_text: Stalactites grow downwards from the roof; stalagmites grow upwards from the floor (CO2 degassing from dripping cave water precipitates successive calcite layers)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 3, pp. 48-52); Mahapatra (p. 70)

topic: Glacial Geomorphology: U-Shaped Glacial Troughs
question: The wavy undulations developed in country rocks whenever the region is subjected to severe pressure or stress are known as :
correct_text: U-shaped valley (Glacial plucking and basal abrasion scour pre-existing V-shaped fluvial valleys into steep-walled, flat-bottomed U-troughs)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 4, pp. 58-62); Mahapatra (p. 60)

topic: Coastal Landforms: Wave-Cut Platforms & Sea Cliffs
question: When axial plane of a fold is vertical and either of the limbs have the same amount of dip then such fold is described as :
correct_text: Wave-cut platform (Sub-horizontal rocky bench formed at the intertidal base of retreating sea cliffs by hydraulic wave hammering)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 4, pp. 62-66); Mahapatra (p. 80)

topic: Volcanic Landforms: Basaltic Shield Volcanoes
question: The horizontal component of the apparent displacement of a bed, measured along the direction of dip of the fault is known as :
correct_text: Low-viscosity fluid basaltic lava flows (Effusive eruptions of hot Hawaiian tholeiitic lavas travel extensive distances, building broad gentle domes)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 4, pp. 65-70); Bangar (p. 74)

topic: Structural Geology: Rock Outcrop Exposure
question: Apart of any stream or rock that is exposed at the surface is known as :
correct_text: Outcrop (A direct exposure of solid bedrock visible on the Earth's surface through unweathered vegetative or superficial cover)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, 2nd Ed., Ch. 1, p. 10); Bangar (p. 170)

topic: Dip-Slip Fault Kinematics: Reverse Fault Geometry
question: In a dip-slip fault, if the hanging wall block moved up relative to the footwall block, then the fault is classified as :
correct_text: Reverse fault (A dip-slip fault where compressive horizontal stress drives the hanging wall block upward relative to the footwall)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 16, pp. 360-375); Bangar (p. 192)

topic: Fold Geometry: Arch-Shaped Upward Antiforms
question: The crest of fold where strata are bent up to form an arch is known as:
correct_text: Anticline (A structural fold convex upward whose limbs dip away from the central hinge line, with oldest strata in the core)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 10, pp. 215-225); Bangar (p. 180)

topic: Fold Hinge Line & Plunging Fold Mechanics
question: How thick is the crust of the Earth ?
correct_text: Hinge line (The line connecting points of maximum geometric curvature on a folded layer surface)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 10, pp. 216-220); Bangar (p. 182)

topic: Fault Terminology: Fault Scarp Geomorphology
question: Which layer separates crust from core ?
correct_text: Fault scarp (A steep topographic step or cliff generated on the ground surface by direct surface rupture displacement along a fault)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 8, pp. 165-170); Keller (p. 120)

topic: Joint Taxonomy: Strike Joints vs Dip Joints
question: Whatdrives the Earth’s internal heat engine ?
correct_text: Strike joints are parallel to regional strike; dip joints are parallel to dip (Systematic fracture sets aligned with principal kinematic axes)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 7, pp. 140-148); Bangar (p. 202)

topic: Fault Gouge vs Mylonite: Brittle vs Ductile Zones
question: Which of the following compound is most abundant in earth crust ?
correct_text: Fault gouge forms under brittle frictional crushing; mylonite forms under ductile crystal-plastic shearing (Depth and temperature dictate the brittle-ductile transition)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 8 & 15, pp. 170-345); Ramsay & Huber

topic: Igneous Petrography: Granite Mineralogical Composition
question: Whichis the last mineral to crystallize from a magma in Bowen’s reaction series ?
correct_text: Quartz, K-feldspar, plagioclase, and biotite/hornblende (A coarse-grained felsic plutonic rock with >20% modal quartz on the QAPF diagram)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 2, pp. 25-30); Bangar (p. 96)

topic: Basalt Petrogenesis: Mid-Ocean Ridge Tholeiite (MORB)
question: What is the volcanic equivalent of the gabbro ?
correct_text: Partial melting of depleted upper mantle peridotite (Decompression melting of lherzolite/harzburgite below spreading axes generates N-MORB melts)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous Petrology, Ch. 13, pp. 260-275); Kearey

topic: Metamorphic Facies: Barrow's Regional Metamorphic Zones
question: Who is the father of modern geochemistry ?
correct_text: Chlorite -> Biotite -> Garnet -> Staurolite -> Kyanite -> Sillimanite (Classic orogenic medium-P/T Barrovian index mineral sequence in pelitic protoliths)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, pp. 425-430); Bangar (p. 130)

topic: Contact Metamorphism: Thermal Aureoles & Hornfels
question: Name the chemistry that deals with geological process at the “atomic level” and the history of atoms in the | earth’s crust and on the planet as a whole :
correct_text: Hornfels (Non-foliated, fine-grained granoblastic rock produced by thermal recrystallization in the inner aureole surrounding plutonic intrusions)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, pp. 422-426); Bangar (p. 134)

topic: Sedimentary Petrography: Quartz Arenite Maturity
question: Thecomposition, structure, process and other physical aspects of Earth are studied by:
correct_text: High mineralogical and textural maturity (>95% framework quartz, well-sorted, rounded grains reflecting prolonged abrasive transport)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 5, pp. 120-128); Bangar (p. 142)

topic: Carbonate Petrography: Folk Classification (Allochems)

question: The migration of the oil from the reservoir to the trap is known as :
correct_text: API = (141.5 / SG at 60 °F) - 131.5 (Inversely proportional to specific gravity; higher API gravity indicates lighter, more valuable crude oil)
textbook_ref: Richard C. Selley (Elements of Petroleum Geology, Ch. 2, pp. 25-30)

topic: Caprock Sealing Integrity in Petroleum Geology
question: The layer containing petroleum oil and gas is :
correct_text: Ductile, thick, impermeable shale or bedded halite with high capillary entry pressure preventing buoyant hydrocarbon leakage
textbook_ref: Richard C. Selley (Elements of Petroleum Geology, Ch. 7, pp. 300-315)

topic: Coal Petrography: Vitrinite Reflectance Thermal Maturity
question: Boiling point of fuel oil is :
correct_text: Percentage of incident light reflected by vitrinite under oil immersion (Standard optical benchmark for coal rank and oil/gas window maturity)
textbook_ref: Richard C. Selley (Elements of Petroleum Geology, Ch. 5, pp. 195-202); Stach

topic: Coal Chemistry: Proximate vs Ultimate Analysis
question: Dead organisms are transformed into petroleum and natural gas in :
correct_text: Proximate determines moisture, volatile matter, fixed carbon, and ash; ultimate determines C, H, N, S, and O elemental percentages
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 13, pp. 266-268); Selley

topic: Economic Commodities: Petroleum as 'Black Gold'
question: What is called Black Gold ?
correct_text: Petroleum (Crude oil is universally referred to as 'Black Gold' due to its supreme global economic, industrial, and strategic value)
textbook_ref: Richard C. Selley (Elements of Petroleum Geology, Ch. 1, pp. 1-8); Bangar (p. 270)
